story.title: Russian Projectile Explosion in Lviv Kills Two and Injures Ten
story.summary: A Russian projectile struck a building in Lviv, resulting in the deaths of two individuals and injuring at least ten others. The incident was captured on a dashcam, showing the moment of the explosion as a car was forced to reverse to avoid the blast.

explore_lenses.label: Why did the Lviv strike disrupt more than one site?
explore_lenses.title: Rail and power effects widened the impact
explore_lenses.summary: The casualties were concentrated at Lviv's Sknyliv railway station, but the same attack also affected regional energy infrastructure, extending the consequences to transport and electricity service.

claims.text: Lviv regional authorities said the Sknyliv station was the location with the most casualties and that its ticket offices were damaged.
Police reported damage to an energy-infrastructure facility in Stryi district and said emergency and scheduled power-outage regimes were introduced in the Lviv region.
The regional administration also reported damage to homes, garages and vehicles in several districts, including damage caused by debris after air-defense interceptions.

points: Lviv regional authorities said the Sknyliv station was the location with the most casualties and that its ticket offices were damaged.
Police reported damage to an energy-infrastructure facility in Stryi district and said emergency and scheduled power-outage regimes were introduced in the Lviv region.
The regional administration also reported damage to homes, garages and vehicles in several districts, including damage caused by debris after air-defense interceptions.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Officials said damage assessments were still being updated, so the full scale and duration of service disruption were not yet established.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: How did Lviv fit into the wider barrage?
explore_lenses.title: It was part of a large, multi-region attack
explore_lenses.summary: Lviv was one of several regions hit in a coordinated Russian missile-and-drone assault on November 20, rather than an isolated local event.

claims.text: Lviv police and the regional administration said Russian forces attacked the region overnight and in the morning with missiles and drones; air defenses operated for nearly six hours, according to the regional administration.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 400 attack drones and over 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, across multiple Ukrainian cities and regions.

Zelenskyy said the missiles were launched in groups separated by 20–30-minute intervals, which he argued complicated firefighting, rubble clearance and repairs; this characterization has not been independently assessed in the cited official reporting.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for recovery and accountability?
explore_lenses.title: Repairs and a war-crimes investigation are underway
explore_lenses.summary: Local agencies are clearing damage and collecting evidence, while Ukrainian leaders are pressing partners for more air-defense supplies to reduce exposure to future missile attacks.

claims.text: Lviv police said law-enforcement officers, rescuers and other services were continuing consequence-management work, while police collected physical evidence at the attack sites.

Investigators from the Security Service of Ukraine in Lviv region, under the regional prosecutor's supervision, opened a pretrial investigation under Article 438 of Ukraine's Criminal Code concerning war crimes, police said.

Zelenskyy said restoration work was under way where security conditions permitted and called on partner governments to accelerate agreed air-defense deliveries, particularly interceptor missiles for ballistic threats.

story_report.summary: A Russian projectile explosion in Lviv killed two people and injured at least 10, according to reports cited by Africanews and Euronews. Dashcam footage captured the blast as a car reversed away from the scene. Regional authorities and police said Russian forces attacked the wider Lviv region overnight and into the morning with missiles and drones, while air defenses operated for nearly six hours.

sections.heading: Lviv Transport and Power Damage
sections.body: Regional authorities said Sknyliv station had the most casualties and that its ticket offices were damaged. Police also reported damage to an energy-infrastructure facility in Stryi district, prompting emergency and scheduled power-outage regimes across the Lviv region. The regional administration reported additional damage to homes, garages and vehicles in several districts, including from debris after air-defense interceptions.

sections.heading: Zelenskyy Describes Wider Russian Barrage
sections.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 400 attack drones and over 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, against multiple Ukrainian cities and regions. He said the missiles were fired in groups separated by 20 to 30 minutes, which he argued complicated firefighting, rubble clearance and repairs. The stated launch totals and that characterization were not independently assessed in the cited official reporting.

sections.heading: Lviv Investigators Open War-Crimes Case
sections.body: Police said rescuers, law-enforcement officers and other services continued managing the consequences of the attacks while officers collected physical evidence at affected sites. Security Service investigators in the Lviv region, supervised by the regional prosecutor’s office, opened a pretrial investigation under Article 438 of Ukraine’s Criminal Code concerning war crimes. Zelenskyy said restoration work was under way where security conditions allowed and urged partners to speed delivery of air-defense systems and interceptor missiles.

unresolved.text: Officials were still updating damage assessments, leaving the full scale of damage and the duration of service disruptions unestablished.

Public reports did not identify the specific munition responsible for each damaged site, and no final casualty count, repair-completion timetable or public finding of individual criminal responsibility was available.

related_stories.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Condemns Attacks on Palestinian Villages as 'Jewish Terrorism'
related_stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank, labeling them as 'Jewish terrorism.' The attacks involved Israeli settlers setting fire to vehicles and properties in multiple locations. In response, Israeli authorities have initiated an investigation into the incidents.

related_stories.title: Capture of Cartel Leader 'El Chapo Isidro' Sparks Violence in Sinaloa
related_stories.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, was captured by Mexican special forces in Sinaloa during a military operation. Following his arrest, violence erupted in the region, resulting in at least 11 deaths, with reports of gunfire and chaos among civilians. The operation involved cooperation with US intelligence and included a shootout between security forces and armed members of his cartel.

related_stories.title: FBI Investigates Possible Hack of National Crime Information Center Database
related_stories.summary: The FBI is reportedly investigating a potential hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database, which is utilized by various law enforcement agencies to share critical criminal justice information. The NCIC contains records on fugitives, missing persons, and stolen property, among other data.

related_stories.title: Fire at Indonesian Confectionery Factory Leaves Three Dead and Dozens Missing
related_stories.summary: A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta, Indonesia, has resulted in at least three fatalities, with 36 individuals reported missing. The blaze, which began in a cooling unit on the third floor, has left parts of the factory severely damaged, including a collapsed roof. Firefighters continue to battle the flames more than 12 hours after the incident started, while rescue efforts are underway to locate the missing persons.
